course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Polynomial and Rational Functions
unit.description: See how outputs change with inputs, then use rates of change, zeros, end behavior, asymptotes, and holes to describe polynomial and rational functions and build models from them.

topic.title: Transformations of Functions
topic.summary: Additive and multiplicative transformations: translations, dilations, and reflections, combined transformations, and their effect on domain, range, and asymptotes.

questions.prompt: The function g is given by g(x) = f(x − 4) + 1. Which of the following describes how the graph of g is related to the graph of f?
choices: A horizontal translation by 4 units and a vertical translation by 1 unit
A horizontal translation by −4 units and a vertical translation by 1 unit
A horizontal translation by 1 unit and a vertical translation by 4 units
A horizontal translation by −1 unit and a vertical translation by −4 units
questions.explanation: f(x + h) translates horizontally by −h units. Here h = −4, so the horizontal translation is by 4 units. Adding 1 translates vertically by 1 unit.
choiceExplanations: f(x − 4) is f(x + h) with h = −4, a horizontal translation by 4 units.
The horizontal translation is by −h = 4 units, not −4.
This swaps the two constants.
Both translations are reversed.
questions.distinguisher: g(x) = f(x + h) translates by −h units, so the sign flips.

questions.prompt: The point (2, 5) is on the graph of the function f. Which of the following points must be on the graph of g(x) = f(x + 3) − 2?
questions.explanation: g(x) = f(x + 3) − 2 needs x + 3 = 2, so x = −1, and g(−1) = f(2) − 2 = 3. The point (−1, 3) is on the graph of g.
choiceExplanations: x = 5 gives f(8), not f(2). The horizontal translation is by −3 units.
The horizontal part is right, but the output value is f(2) − 2 = 3.
Both translations are reversed.
questions.distinguisher: Solve for the input value that makes x + 3 equal the original x-coordinate.

questions.prompt: Which of the following functions g is a reflection of the graph of f over the x-axis?
questions.explanation: g(x) = a·f(x) with a = −1 is a vertical dilation by a factor of 1 with a reflection over the x-axis.
choiceExplanations: f(−x) is f(bx) with b = −1, a reflection over the y-axis.
Multiplying the output values by −1 reflects the graph over the x-axis.
1/f(x) is not a transformation of this kind.
Multiplying by −x is not a constant multiple, so it is not a dilation.
questions.distinguisher: A negative multiplier on the output reflects over the x-axis. On the input, it reflects over the y-axis.

questions.prompt: The point (6, −4) is on the graph of the function f. Which of the following points must be on the graph of h(x) = f(x/3)?
questions.explanation: h(x) = f(bx) with b = 1/3 is a horizontal dilation by a factor of 3. x/3 = 6 gives x = 18, and h(18) = f(6) = −4.
choiceExplanations: A horizontal dilation by a factor of 1/|b| = 3 multiplies x-coordinates by 3.
A horizontal dilation does not change the output values.
Only the input is changed, so the output value stays −4.
x/3 = 6 gives x = 18, and the output value is still −4.
questions.distinguisher: f(bx) dilates horizontally by 1/|b|, not by |b|.

questions.prompt: The table gives values of the function f for selected values of x. Let g(x) = a·f(bx) + c, where a, b, and c are constants. The graph of g is constructed by applying three transformations to the graph of f in this order: a horizontal dilation by a factor of 1/2, a vertical dilation by a factor of 2, and a vertical translation by −3 units. What is the value of g(−1)?
questions.explanation: A horizontal dilation by a factor of 1/2 means b = 2, so g(x) = 2f(2x) − 3. Then g(−1) = 2f(−2) − 3 = 2(1) − 3 = −1.
choiceExplanations: This translates by 3 units instead of −3 units: 2f(−2) + 3 = 5.
This translates before dilating: 2(f(−2) − 3) = −4. The vertical translation is applied last.
This ignores the horizontal dilation: 2f(−1) − 3 = 11.
questions.distinguisher: A horizontal dilation by a factor of 1/2 corresponds to f(2x).

questions.prompt: The graph of g is the graph of f reflected over the x-axis, then translated horizontally by −2 units and vertically by 5 units. Which of the following is an expression for g(x)?
questions.explanation: A reflection over the x-axis gives −f(x). A horizontal translation by −2 units replaces x with x + 2, and a vertical translation by 5 adds 5: g(x) = −f(x + 2) + 5.
choiceExplanations: f(x − 2) is a horizontal translation by 2 units, not −2.
A negative sign on the input reflects over the y-axis.
This has no horizontal translation.
f(x + h) with h = 2 translates by −2 units.
questions.distinguisher: A horizontal translation by −2 units is f(x + 2).

questions.prompt: The function g is given by g(x) = 1/(x − 2) + 3. Which of the following are the equations of the asymptotes of the graph of g?
questions.explanation: The parent function 1/x has asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0. A horizontal translation by 2 units moves the vertical asymptote to x = 2, and a vertical translation by 3 units moves the horizontal asymptote to y = 3.
choiceExplanations: 1/(x − 2) is a horizontal translation by 2 units, so the vertical asymptote is x = 2.
Adding 3 translates the horizontal asymptote up to y = 3.
The vertical asymptote is x = 2 and the horizontal asymptote is y = 3.
The constants are swapped.
questions.distinguisher: Vertical asymptotes move with horizontal translations, and horizontal asymptotes move with vertical ones.

questions.prompt: The function f(x) = x² has range y ≥ 0. What is the range of h(x) = −2f(x) + 3?
questions.explanation: f(x) ≥ 0 gives −2f(x) ≤ 0, so h(x) = −2f(x) + 3 ≤ 3. The greatest value, 3, occurs at x = 0.
choiceExplanations: The factor −2 reflects the graph over the x-axis, so the inequality reverses.
The vertical translation is by 3 units, not −3.
The reflection reverses the inequality, and the translation is by 3, not −3.
questions.distinguisher: Apply the output transformations to y ≥ 0 in order, and reverse the inequality when multiplying by a negative.

questions.prompt: A student claims that the graph of g(x) = f(x + 3) is the graph of f translated horizontally by 3 units, because the constant 3 is added. Which of the following is the best response?
choices: The claim is incorrect: g(x) = f(x + h) is a horizontal translation by −h units, so the translation is by −3 units.
The claim is incorrect: adding 3 to the input translates the graph vertically by 3 units.
The claim is correct: adding a constant to the input translates the graph by that constant.
The claim is incorrect: the graph is dilated horizontally by a factor of 3.
questions.explanation: g(−3) = f(0), so the point (0, f(0)) of f appears at x = −3 on g. The graph is translated horizontally by −3 units.
choiceExplanations: g(x) = f(x + h) is a horizontal translation by −h units, so f(x + 3) moves the graph by −3 units.
The 3 is added to the input, so the translation is horizontal.
g(−3) = f(0), so points move by −3 units, not 3.
Adding to the input translates the graph. Multiplying the input dilates it.
questions.distinguisher: Test one point: where does (0, f(0)) appear on g?

questions.prompt: The population, in millions, of a town t years after 2020 is modeled by P(t). A second town follows the same pattern 5 years later and is modeled by Q(t) = P(t − 5). Which of the following is the best interpretation?
choices: The second town's population is 5 million more than the first town's.
The second town's population is 5 times the first town's at every time t.
The second town reaches each value 5 years before the first town does.
The second town reaches each population value 5 years after the first town does.
questions.explanation: Q(t) = P(t − 5) is a horizontal translation by 5 units. Q(7) = P(2), so the value the first town has at t = 2 occurs for the second town at t = 7, 5 years later.
choiceExplanations: A vertical translation would be P(t) + 5.
A vertical dilation would be 5·P(t).
The translation is by 5 units to the right, so events happen later, not earlier.
Q(t) = P(t − 5) shifts each value 5 years later.
questions.distinguisher: A horizontal translation by a positive amount delays every value.
